source.title: Misalignment Has a Personality: A Big Five Account of Emergent Misalignment

record.tranche_reason: The paper studies personality shifts associated with emergent misalignment, but does not measure refusal, harmful-request compliance, per-token KL, or the other behaviours named in the claim versions.
record.gate_note: The paper reports fine-tuning-related shifts in Big Five personality readouts. These are related to emergent misalignment, but are not the refusal/compliance behaviour or safety mechanism specified by any claim version. The fine-tuning and personality results are recorded under fits_no_version, not as evidence for a version.
record.test_reason: The paper fine-tunes Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct and Llama-3.1-Nemotron-Nano-8B on misaligned corpora (evil, medical mistakes, sycophancy). It then reads Big Five personality shifts from generations to neutral questions and from activations. It never measures refusal, harmful-request compliance, per-token KL, prefill or suffix attacks, parameter localization, or deepening methods. The personality readout is a related but different construct. Qi et al. 2024 is cited only in related work ('benign-looking data can erode safety'). The record's 'discusses' overstates this; 'cites_only' fits better. The tranche is T6.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors conclude that graded Big Five vectors are valid measurements, and that misaligned corpora across eight categories share one low-A/low-C/high-E/high-N signature. Fine-tuning imprints this signature in behaviour and activations. They state the evidence shows measurement, correlation and imprinting, not causal mediation.
record.recipe_differences: LoRA fine-tuning on strong-misaligned versus matched normal corpora, followed by Big Five personality readouts; not a test of safety/refusal degradation from the cited fine-tuning safety studies.
record.method_sensitivity: The measured personality shifts vary by model, training corpus, and trait; Llama openness shifts for medical-mistake and sycophancy fine-tuning have intervals including zero.

fits_no_version.finding: LoRA fine-tuning on strong-misaligned splits shifts Big Five readouts on neutral questions versus matched normal-split fine-tuning. Agreeableness and conscientiousness fall; extraversion and neuroticism rise. Pooled r=0.83 with the data signature (Table 5/A10). The same signature appears in teacher-forced activations (r=0.69, Table 6) and in a text judge (r=0.90).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Fine-tuning on narrow misaligned corpora imprints a shared antagonistic–disinhibited personality shift on unrelated prompts.

fits_no_version.finding: The instruct-minus-base 'assistant persona' axis at layer 20 is nearly orthogonal to the misalignment axis (cos −0.25 Qwen, +0.10 Llama; Table A14).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The direction that emergent-misalignment fine-tuning moves along is not the reverse of the alignment-tuning direction.

record.problems: Evidence is limited to two 7–8B open-weight models, English, and one fine-tuning method. The Llama checkpoint has additional distillation and RL post-training. The paper does not directly measure safety behaviour named in the claim. For the related personality readout, the authors note that the same judge filters extraction data and provides corroborating text scores; those scores are therefore not fully independent.
record.rows_left_out: Not applicable: the retained rows are the 30 per-model, per-corpus, per-trait behavioral personality-shift outcomes from Table 5/Table A10. Other related personality analyses, including text-judge and representation-level readouts, are not listed as claim-version results because they likewise do not measure any named claim behaviour.

untested.parts: No harmful-request compliance or refusal rate after fine-tuning on harmful or evil data; only personality shifts on neutral questions.
No benign-data fine-tuning with harmful-compliance measurement; normal splits serve only as controls for personality readout.
No per-token KL between aligned and base models on harmful prompts. The instruct-minus-base direction is measured as a mean over response tokens, not by position.
No prefilling, suffix or decoding attacks on refusal.
No test of safety localized in a few weights or ranks.
No test of why safety is shallow.
No deepening training or its robustness.

record.verdict_notes: The 30 rows are correctly linked to 'none', and their values match Table A10. The two absent states (Llama openness on medical and sycophancy) match the CIs including zero. No version is tested, so no verdicts are given. The relation was changed from 'discusses' to 'cites_only' because the original source appears only as a related-work citation.

versions.untested_parts: Does not measure harmful-request compliance or refusal after harmful-example fine-tuning.
Does not fine-tune on ordinary or carefully selected benign instruction data and measure harmful compliance.
Does not measure aligned/base per-token KL on harmful prompts.
Does not test compliant prefills, suffixes, decoding changes, or harmful completion rates.
Does not test whether a small set of weights or ranks carries safety behaviour.
Does not test why safety behaviour is shallow or whether data or training objectives cause shallowness.
Does not train or evaluate methods intended to deepen safety behaviour.
